messages:
marta: quick heads-up — EU hourly aggregates show a 6hr freshness gap starting ~03:15 UTC, looks correlated with late-ingest from our kafka EU region. thinking we should run a targeted resample backfill with lower sample-rate first. any objections?
ashok: +1 on targeted. prefer sampling over full recompute. reduces cost and avoids tripping quota guardrails.
liam: can we restrict to 'session_events' and only tenants hitting >1% freshness drop? otherwise we'll waste GPU slots.
sienna: that filter sounds good. also + please run a canary for a single shard/tenant before wide roll.
marta: plan: 1) dry-run resample on shard eu-3 for acme-inc 2) sample-rate 25% 3) check agg-diff dashboard and keys per tenant 4) if good, run rolling resample with 2% increments and a 30m watch window.
devon: nit: use our fair-share lane flag so this doesn't steal reclaimed slots. add `--priority resample-low` so it respects quota. ops-bot will still alert if preempted.
ashok: command i was thinking to dry-run:
```
./replayer \
  --env eu \
  --shard eu-3 \
  --tenant acme-inc \
  --table session_events \
  --from 2026-03-18T00:00Z \
  --to   2026-03-19T00:00Z \
  --sample-rate 0.25 \
  --dry-run \
  --priority resample-low
```
liam: looks good. after dry-run post these checks: 1) per-tenant token delta 2) aggregate drift pct 3) query latency impact on leader nodes. If any >5%/10s, abort.
sienna: console UX note — the resample slider uses percents but our API expects float 0-1. pls ensure the console converts and shows the effective predicted token cost estimate. users keep mistyping 25 -> 2500.
marta: good catch. i'll open a tiny console tweak ticket after the run.
devon: ops-bot: create run and tag as canary-3732109999?
ops-bot: created run id run_2026_3732109999 (status: scheduled). watchers: @marta @ashok @liam. ETA start: 2026-03-20T03:45Z UTC.
ashok: when rolling, let's also enable KV-prefix caching for the canary to see hit-rate improvements — that should reduce repeated decode cost.
liam: agree. enable `cache:prefix` and capture metrics: kv_hit_rate, per-token-ms, and s3-reads. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/telemetry/resample?run=run_2026_3732109999
sienna: If the canary looks clean we should still cap the global ramp at 10% of reserved capacity per hour. last time we pushed too fast and tripped the priority lane swap.
marta: fine — ramp policy: 10% reserved/hr, rollback on >3% aggregate drift or >3s p95 latency regression. will monitor on-call channel.
devon: reminder: team quotas apply. if we need extra capacity request via #eng-sre with tag `resample-burst` and cc @liam.
ashok: after the canary, if we go wide, propose using shard-affinity routing policy to spread traffic evenly (avoid hot-sharding). else we get transient hotspots.
liam: +1. Also add a note in the backfill run metadata: "sampling_strategy=adaptive, fallback=full-recompute" so ops can decide fallback plan.
marta: ok kicking off dry-run now. i'll post results summary here within the hour. :rocket:
ops-bot: run_2026_3732109999 changed to running (canary). logs: https://ops.redwood.ai/runs/run_2026_3732109999/logs
marta: quick interim — dry-run completed, no >5% drift, kv_hit_rate ~0.18, p95 token-ms +0.6s. proceeding to hourly 10% ramp.
sienna: great, tagging console tweak ticket as follow-up: CONS-9287 so UI shows float->percent conversion and a cost-estimate tooltip.
devon: i'll open an eng-sre ticket to temporarily bump quota for resample-low lane if we need headroom.
liam: thanks all. once full sweep completes let's snapshot the dashboard and store eval prompt sets so QA can validate user-visible regressions.
marta: done. summary and artifacts saved to https://docs.redwood.ai/backfills/resample-3732109999. closing thread when the run finishes. :white_check_mark:
